facts.text: Hypersensitivity to any component of the lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide tablet.
History of angioedema related to previous ACE‑inhibitor therapy, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema.
Anuria or hypersensitivity to sulfonamide‑derived drugs (due to the hydrochlorothiazide component).
facts.population: Patients with anuria or sulfonamide allergy

facts.text: Concomitant use of neprilysin inhibitors (e.g., sacubitril) or administration within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan.
Coadministration of aliskiren in patients with diabetes.

Angioedema of the face, lips, tongue, glottis or larynx may occur at any time; higher incidence in Black patients; can be fatal due to airway obstruction. Discontinue immediately and provide airway management.
Intestinal angioedema presenting with abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; resolves after stopping the drug.
Anaphylactoid reactions reported during hymenoptera venom desensitization, high‑flux dialysis, or LDL‑apheresis; may be life‑threatening. Stop the drug and treat aggressively.
facts.population: Patients undergoing desensitization, dialysis, or apheresis

facts.text: Excessive hypotension, especially in volume‑depleted, diuretic‑treated, or dialysis patients; syncope reported (0.8% combination, 0.1% lisinopril alone). Monitor blood pressure and consider volume expansion.
facts.population: Patients on diuretics, dialysis, or with severe CHF

facts.text: Rare neutropenia/agranulocytosis; consider periodic white‑blood‑cell monitoring in patients with collagen‑vascular disease or renal disease.
facts.population: Patients with collagen‑vascular disease or renal impairment

facts.text: Rare hepatic injury (cholestatic jaundice, hepatitis, fulminant necrosis). Discontinue if jaundice or marked liver‑enzyme elevations occur.
Hydrochlorothiazide may cause acute transient myopia and secondary angle‑closure glaucoma; discontinue the thiazide component promptly if visual symptoms develop.

Fetal toxicity when used in the second or third trimester; can cause oligohydramnios, fetal renal failure, lung hypoplasia, skeletal deformations, neonatal hypotension, anuria, renal failure, or death. Discontinue immediately if pregnancy is detected.
Lisinopril monotherapy: 10–80 mg once daily. Hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy: 12.5–50 mg daily.
Combination therapy: lisinopril 10–80 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 6.25–50 mg. Initial doses 10‑12.5 mg or 20‑12.5 mg; increase hydrochlorothiazide no sooner than 2–3 weeks. Maximum dose 80 mg/50 mg.
No dose adjustment required if creatinine clearance >30 mL/min/1.73 m² (serum creatinine ≤3 mg/dL). In severe renal impairment, avoid the combination and use a loop diuretic instead.
Elderly patients exhibit ~120% higher AUC for lisinopril and ~80% higher AUC for hydrochlorothiazide; start at the low end of the dosing range and assess renal function before titration.

Hydrochlorothiazide may precipitate azotemia in severe renal disease; monitor renal function. NSAIDs co‑administered with ACE inhibitors can cause acute renal failure, especially in elderly, volume‑depleted, or renally compromised patients; monitor renal function periodically.
facts.population: Patients with renal disease, elderly, or volume depletion

facts.text: Non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drugs (including COX‑2 inhibitors) may attenuate the antihypertensive effect of lisinopril and worsen renal function; monitor blood pressure and renal parameters.
Dual blockade of the renin‑angiotensin system (ACE inhibitor + ARB or aliskiren) increases risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and acute kidney injury; avoid combined use.
Potassium‑sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, or salt substitutes can cause hyperkalemia when used with lisinopril; monitor serum potassium.
facts.population: All patients, especially those on potassium‑sparing agents

facts.text: Lithium clearance is reduced; serum lithium levels may rise to toxic levels. Monitor lithium concentrations frequently if co‑administered.
mTOR inhibitors (temsirolimus, sirolimus, everolimus) increase the risk of angioedema when combined with lisinopril.
Neprilysin inhibitors increase the risk of angioedema when combined with lisinopril; avoid co‑administration.
Aliskiren is contraindicated with lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide in diabetic patients; avoid co‑administration.
